taxonomyNote: NatureServe calls this species Southern California Slender Salamander but lists Garden Slender Salamander as an alternate name; the desert slender salamander B. aridus is now treated as the subspecies B. m. aridus.
fieldMarks: Slender, worm-like salamander of the genus Batrachoseps.
Slightly wider body and a lighter grey belly than the black-bellied slender salamander; body colour varies widely.
behavior: Nocturnal on the surface, mostly active November-April in cool, wet or humid weather; found under rocks, bark and logs, and formerly common in gardens under stones, boards and potted plants.
Retreats to burrows or underground crevices in sandy or gravelly soil in cold or dry weather.
Terrestrial breeder with no aquatic larval stage; eggs are laid in fall and winter. Feeds on small invertebrates such as insects, spiders, snails and sowbugs.
habitat: Oak woodland, chaparral and grassy slopes in canyons and washes, and rural gardens and urban edges next to natural areas.
Prefers moist areas with rocky cover and is tied to seepages.
range: Southern California from the base of the San Gabriel and San Bernardino mountains south to El Rosario, Baja California, plus Catalina and offshore islands; up to about 1,500 m. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Black-bellied slender salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Black-bellied has a thinner body and may have a lighter dorsal stripe; the garden slender salamander has a slightly wider body and lighter grey belly.
